title: Polynomial associated graded implies regularity in a Noetherian local ring
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring with $1\ne0$, meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal, and assume that $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $b\geq0$, let $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in\mathfrak m$, and put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ and $C=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Suppose that the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_J(A),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ is an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, with M=A; the quasi-regular hypothesis is expanded using Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence.

proof.text: Put J = span(range f). Since every f j belongs to the maximal ideal, J is proper. Hence A/J is nontrivial. Every prefix ideal I_i is contained in J, so A/I_i is a nontrivial Noetherian local quotient ring.

Apply the stated prefix-quotient theorem to obtain a bijective polynomial associated-graded map for the tail g in B=A/I_i. Its coefficient quotient B/K is isomorphic to A/J. Therefore K=span(range g) is proper.

Apply Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing to the proper ideal K in the Noetherian local ring B. This is the local-ring, M=B specialization of the Jacobson Krull-intersection theorem and gives intersection_n K^n=0.

Prove a generic initial-form lemma with separatedness explicit. If a*x=0 and x is in K^n, lift its degree-n class through the bijective polynomial map. Multiplying its preimage by the variable for a maps to the class of a*x, hence to zero, by the associated-graded product formula. Injectivity of the polynomial map and regularity of a polynomial variable make the preimage zero. Thus the degree-n class of x is zero and x lies in K^(n+1). Starting with K^0=B gives x in every power, so separatedness makes x=0. The zero-kernel criterion proves injectivity.

Identify the ideal of List.take i (List.ofFn f) with I_i by the indexed membership descriptions; its product with the full ring module is itself. Transfer injectivity of multiplication by the next tail element to the original A-scalar action. These are exactly the weak-regularity conditions. Mathlib IsRegular.of_isWeaklyRegular_of_mem_maximalIdeal supplies the final nonzero-quotient condition from membership in the maximal ideal. For b=0 the weak-regularity conditions are empty, and the same criterion applies.

proof_origin.place: Tag 061S and Tag 061R. N2 formalization uses induction through all filtration levels for a zero product instead of choosing a least nonzero initial form, and applies Krull intersection directly over the Noetherian local prefix quotient.
